A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Autoencoding Random Forests and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison; the appendix pages are identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction benchmarks, MNIST experiments, genomic analyses, decoder comparisons, and runtime measurements in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Table 1's reconstruction benchmark and Appendix B's supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The RF kernel, diffusion-map encoder, constrained-optimization, split-relabeling and k-NN decoders remain unchanged, as does Appendix C's lasso and greedy-search procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 20 tabular benchmarks, MNIST, mouse-brain transcriptomic datasets, and leukemia dataset for the same reconstruction, visualization and denoising tasks.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain AE, VAE, TVAE and TTVAE in the tabular benchmark, ConvAE in the MNIST comparison, and the same alternative decoders. The new Zhou–Hooker citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The bootstrap/out-of-bag evaluation, compression ratios, distortion metric, model configurations and training budgets are unchanged. Appendix B retains identical experimental protocols.

E4.justification: The decoder comparison, MNIST hyperparameter analyses, supervised-versus-unsupervised comparisons and runtime analyses are retained without revision in Appendix B.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same ten-bootstrap benchmark, five-bootstrap decoder comparison, standard errors and runtime repetition information. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical and qualitative results are unchanged across the main text and appendices. Table 1 retains RFAE's average rank of 1.80 and best mean distortion on 12 of 20 datasets.

T1.justification: Definitions, Theorem 3.4, decoder consistency and uniqueness theorems, and their Appendix A proofs remain unchanged. The added prior-work attribution does not revise these mathematical statements or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion remain unchanged, but Section 3 narrows the novelty assertion surrounding Theorem 3.4 from its properties generally to parts (b) and (c), acknowledging earlier PSD results for a non-adaptive variant.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the reconstruction and genomic results, explanations of alternative decoders' failures, and limitations concerning computational cost and neighbor-count sensitivity remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5 now explicitly identifies an R package and adds a Python implementation link alongside the existing reproduction-code link. Implementation settings, hardware descriptions and appendix details are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Zhou and Hooker's Boulevard paper as reference 109. Sections 2–3 acknowledge its non-adaptive kernel results and distinguish the present contribution; the remaining cited works are retained.

P1.justification: There are localized additions concerning prior work and software access, plus updated author names and affiliations. The section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The author block gains numbered affiliations, and text reflow shifts Figures 3–4 vertically within their pages. Figures and tables retain their content and design; appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v4 improves attribution by acknowledging earlier kernel results and narrowing its novelty assertion, while the added Python implementation link improves software-access guidance. These are limited gains: the methods, theoretical arguments, empirical evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
